html:
On 5 October 1910 republicans in Lisbon, backed by soldiers and sailors, overthrew the monarchy. King Manuel II fled to England and Portugal became a republic.

The monarchy had been weakened by debt, by British pressure that forced Portugal to give up its claim to a belt of Africa in 1890, and by the murder of King Carlos and his heir in Lisbon in 1908. The republicans were strong in the cities.

The First Republic separated church and state and expelled the Jesuits. But it was unstable, with dozens of governments in sixteen years, and joined the First World War at great cost. A military coup ended it in 1926, which led to the rule of Salazar. 5 October is a national holiday. See Portugal and the earlier Liberal Wars.
sum: On 5 October 1910 republicans in Lisbon, backed by soldiers and sailors, overthrew the monarchy. King Manuel II fled to England and Portugal became a republic.
